questions.q: What option does an employee have if they genuinely lost a required receipt?
options: No option exists; the expense can never be claimed
They must ask a coworker to fabricate a replacement receipt
They can sign a missing receipt declaration affirming the expense occurred and the amount is accurate
The expense is automatically approved without any record
questions.explain: Expenses supports a formal missing receipt declaration as a fallback, though repeated use of it is itself a pattern audit rules should catch.

questions.q: What is a payment hold rule used for in this context?
options: It raises an employee's mileage rate automatically
It approves expense reports faster
It deletes an employee's expense history
It can place current or future expense reports on hold company-wide when receipts are overdue
questions.explain: A payment hold rule is a backstop that freezes reimbursement until an employee clears a backlog of missing receipts.

questions.q: What is the key difference between a 'receipt' and an 'attachment' in Oracle Fusion Expenses?
options: A receipt is required proof for a specific dollar amount; an attachment is optional supporting documentation
There is no difference; the terms are interchangeable
An attachment is always required and a receipt is always optional
Receipts can only be attached to approved reports
questions.explain: Receipts are mandatory proof above set thresholds, while attachments like agendas or approval emails are optional unless specifically requested.

questions.q: Why does Oracle Fusion Expenses require itemization for a hotel folio?
options: Because hotels never provide valid receipts
Because one folio total often bundles multiple expense types (room, tax, meals, entertainment) that each need correct policy and GL treatment
Because itemization is only cosmetic and has no accounting effect
Because Accommodations is the only category Oracle allows at all
questions.explain: Itemization splits a bundled receipt total into correctly coded pieces so each component is evaluated against its own policy and posts to the right account.

questions.q: In Priya's itemized hotel folio example, what happened to the $21.00 pay-per-view movie charge?
options: It was itemized separately and flagged as non-reimbursable, excluded from her reimbursement total
It was added on top of the Hotel expense type with no changes
It was converted into mileage
It caused her entire expense report to be rejected
questions.explain: Itemization split out the movie charge as its own line, correctly flagged non-reimbursable instead of being hidden inside the Hotel expense type.
